source: v0 (literature) revised with taxonomy discovery on 401 experiments (discovery_experiment.json)

pattern.title: Design pattern
pattern.q: Which reusable design is this? Primary first; add a second only if the experiment clearly combines two.

multi-benchmark-head-to-head.name: Multi-benchmark head-to-head table
multi-benchmark-head-to-head.def: The proposed method and published baselines are run on several standard datasets or metrics and reported in one main table.
multi-benchmark-head-to-head.include_if: There are several baselines and several datasets or metrics, and no explicit matching of budget or cost.
multi-benchmark-head-to-head.exclude_if: Compute, tokens or parameters are explicitly equalised (budget-matched-comparison), or the method is evaluated along a sweep of cost (quality-cost-frontier).

budget-matched-comparison.name: Budget- or capacity-matched comparison
budget-matched-comparison.def: Methods are compared with compute, tokens, simulator calls, parameters or unique data held equal, so the gain cannot be blamed on extra resources.
budget-matched-comparison.include_if: The design explicitly equalises a resource, or adds a capacity-matched control to rule out 'it is just bigger'.
budget-matched-comparison.exclude_if: The resource is swept continuously and a frontier is plotted (quality-cost-frontier).

quality-cost-frontier.name: Quality-versus-cost frontier sweep
quality-cost-frontier.def: Methods are traced across a range of budgets, compression rates or step counts to compare whole trade-off curves or Pareto fronts.
quality-cost-frontier.include_if: The x-axis is a resource (bitrate, steps, time, tokens, particles) and every method is plotted along it.
quality-cost-frontier.exclude_if: Only the proposed method is swept, to find its own operating point (hyperparameter-sensitivity-sweep).

many-model-leaderboard.name: Many-model benchmark leaderboard
many-model-leaderboard.def: A new benchmark or attack is applied to many existing models in order to characterise the field, not to promote one method.
many-model-leaderboard.include_if: The paper contributes a benchmark, dataset or attack, and the rows are off-the-shelf models.
many-model-leaderboard.exclude_if: The rows include a proposed method that is meant to win (multi-benchmark-head-to-head).

human-and-qualitative-comparison.name: Human preference or side-by-side qualitative comparison
human-and-qualitative-comparison.def: Outputs of competing methods are judged by people (pairwise preference, expert ratings) or shown side by side in curated visual comparisons.
human-and-qualitative-comparison.include_if: The evidence is human judgments or curated visual galleries comparing methods.
human-and-qualitative-comparison.exclude_if: People are used to validate a metric or a judge rather than to compare methods (measurement-validity).

leave-one-out-ablation.name: Leave-one-out component ablation
leave-one-out-ablation.def: Each module, loss term or reward is removed from the full system in turn, and the drop is measured.
leave-one-out-ablation.include_if: The design is 'full method minus X' for one or more X, starting from the full system.
leave-one-out-ablation.exclude_if: Components are added cumulatively from a base (additive-buildup-ablation), or X is replaced by a specific alternative (component-substitution).

additive-buildup-ablation.name: Cumulative build-up ablation
additive-buildup-ablation.def: Components or training stages are added one at a time to a baseline, and the increment from each is reported.
additive-buildup-ablation.include_if: The table rows build up from a base toward the full method, or add modules onto external baselines.
additive-buildup-ablation.exclude_if: The design starts from the full system and removes parts (leave-one-out-ablation).

component-substitution.name: Component substitution / design-choice swap
component-substitution.def: A design choice is swapped for named alternatives (latent space, masking rule, selection criterion, objective form), keeping everything else fixed.
component-substitution.include_if: Each condition replaces one choice with another concrete option, not with nothing.
component-substitution.exclude_if: The swapped part is outside the method (judge, backend, reward model), so the question is robustness (evaluator-and-infrastructure-swap).

confound-isolating-control.name: Confound-isolating control
confound-isolating-control.def: A control condition separates the claimed cause from a plausible confound: the same data under SFT versus RL, an oracle input, interaction versus static examples, or a matched random subspace.
confound-isolating-control.include_if: The question is phrased as 'is it X or merely Y?' and one condition removes X while keeping Y.
confound-isolating-control.exclude_if: It is a plain removal with no named rival explanation (leave-one-out-ablation).

hyperparameter-sensitivity-sweep.name: Hyperparameter sensitivity sweep
hyperparameter-sensitivity-sweep.def: One method's own hyperparameter (β, depth, step size, threshold, K) is swept to show a stable range or an optimum.
hyperparameter-sensitivity-sweep.include_if: Only one method's configuration varies along a scalar knob.
hyperparameter-sensitivity-sweep.exclude_if: The knob is model or data scale and the goal is a trend or law (scaling-and-extrapolation), or competitors are plotted along the knob (quality-cost-frontier).

input-perturbation-stress-test.name: Input perturbation / corruption stress test
input-perturbation-stress-test.def: Inputs or side information are corrupted on purpose (noise, JPEG, attacks, label masking, swapped partitions, paraphrased prompts) at graded severity.
input-perturbation-stress-test.include_if: A controlled degradation is applied to inputs or supervision, and performance retention is measured.
input-perturbation-stress-test.exclude_if: The shift is a different natural dataset or domain (cross-dataset-replication).

evaluator-and-infrastructure-swap.name: Evaluator, seed and infrastructure stability
evaluator-and-infrastructure-swap.def: Something outside the method is varied (judge model, reward model, scoring rule, random seed, black-box solver, number of runs) to check that rankings or fits are stable.
evaluator-and-infrastructure-swap.include_if: The varied element is part of the measurement or execution pipeline, not the method.
evaluator-and-infrastructure-swap.exclude_if: The varied element is a design choice of the method (component-substitution).

cross-dataset-replication.name: Cross-dataset / cross-domain replication
cross-dataset-replication.def: The main comparison is re-run on another dataset, domain or real-world setting to show the result replicates.
cross-dataset-replication.include_if: The method and baselines stay the same, and the data or domain changes.
cross-dataset-replication.exclude_if: The architecture or backbone changes (cross-backbone-transfer), or the model is trained on one split and tested zero-shot on another (held-out-split-extrapolation).

cross-backbone-transfer.name: Cross-backbone / cross-architecture transfer
cross-backbone-transfer.def: The method is applied unchanged to a different base model, backbone, generator family or system scale.
cross-backbone-transfer.include_if: The base model or architecture is swapped while the method stays fixed.
cross-backbone-transfer.exclude_if: The new setting is a different task family (module-transplant).

held-out-split-extrapolation.name: Train-on-one, test-on-unseen split
held-out-split-extrapolation.def: Training is restricted to one source (a dataset, sequence length, opponent set or model type), and evaluation is on held-out conditions.
held-out-split-extrapolation.include_if: The train and test conditions are explicitly disjoint by design, including length extrapolation.
held-out-split-extrapolation.exclude_if: The method is simply re-run end-to-end on another dataset (cross-dataset-replication).

module-transplant.name: Module transplant into another system or task
module-transplant.def: One proposed ingredient is inserted into a different model or a different task to show it is a general improvement.
module-transplant.include_if: A single component, not the whole method, is ported to a foreign host.
module-transplant.exclude_if: The whole method moves to a new backbone (cross-backbone-transfer).

scale-trend-sweep.name: Scale sweep for trend or optimum
scale-trend-sweep.def: Model size, data amount, generation length, batch size or task count is swept to reveal a trend or a scale-dependent optimum.
scale-trend-sweep.include_if: The sweep is over a size or amount, and the claim is how the outcome changes with it.
scale-trend-sweep.exclude_if: A parametric fit is used to predict unseen scales (fit-and-extrapolate).

fit-and-extrapolate.name: Fit early, predict later
fit-and-extrapolate.def: A functional form is fitted on small or early runs and checked against held-out larger or later runs.
fit-and-extrapolate.include_if: A fitted curve is evaluated on scales it was not fitted on.

resource-complexity-profiling.name: Resource cost vs problem size profiling
resource-complexity-profiling.def: Runtime, memory or overhead is measured as input size grows, or under deployment engines, to establish efficiency.
resource-complexity-profiling.include_if: The outcome is wall-clock, memory or FLOPs rather than quality.
resource-complexity-profiling.exclude_if: Quality is plotted against cost for several methods (quality-cost-frontier).

theory-prediction-overlay.name: Simulation vs theoretical prediction overlay
theory-prediction-overlay.def: Empirical curves from controlled simulations are overlaid on the predicted rates, bounds or equilibria across parameter sweeps.
theory-prediction-overlay.include_if: A theorem's quantitative prediction is plotted against measurements.
theory-prediction-overlay.exclude_if: The theory is only qualitatively illustrated with a constructed case (constructed-counterexample).

constructed-counterexample.name: Constructed toy counterexample
constructed-counterexample.def: A minimal hand-built environment or graph exhibits a predicted failure or disagreement.
constructed-counterexample.include_if: A single designed instance proves existence (policies disagree, work blows up, the update fails).
constructed-counterexample.exclude_if: The result is a parametric sweep against a prediction (theory-prediction-overlay).

planted-ground-truth-recovery.name: Planted ground-truth recovery
planted-ground-truth-recovery.def: Known signals (real images among synthetic ones, true inputs among noise, an exact conjugate posterior) are planted, and recovery is scored.
planted-ground-truth-recovery.include_if: Success is measured against a planted target the method does not see.
planted-ground-truth-recovery.exclude_if: The ground truth is a theoretical rate rather than a planted object (theory-prediction-overlay).

representation-probing.name: Probing and representation similarity
representation-probing.def: Linear probes, CCA or RSA, or classifiers on activations measure what information representations encode or how similar they are.
representation-probing.include_if: The output is a readout or similarity score computed from frozen activations.
representation-probing.exclude_if: Activations are edited and behaviour is re-measured (causal-internal-intervention).

causal-internal-intervention.name: Causal intervention on internals with matched controls
causal-internal-intervention.def: A subspace, head or update component is erased, restored or amplified, and the behavioural effect is compared with matched random controls.
causal-internal-intervention.include_if: Internal states are edited at inference or in the optimiser, and the downstream effect is measured.
causal-internal-intervention.exclude_if: Whole modules of the method are removed and the model is retrained (leave-one-out-ablation).

internals-visualization.name: Visualizing learned internals over training
internals-visualization.def: t-SNE or PCA, attention maps, routing traces or learned weight maps are plotted to show qualitative structure or how it evolves.
internals-visualization.include_if: The evidence is mainly a visualization of internal quantities, without an intervention.
internals-visualization.exclude_if: A quantitative probe or a statistical test is the main evidence (representation-probing).

targeted-quantity-check.name: Verify the method moves its target quantity
targeted-quantity-check.def: The method is checked to change the intermediate quantity its motivation names (gradient variance, redundant tokens, alignment score, smoothness).
targeted-quantity-check.include_if: The outcome is the mediator posited by the method or theory, not the end metric.
targeted-quantity-check.exclude_if: The mediator is correlated across many checkpoints without the method being applied (metric-outcome-correlation).

failure-taxonomy.name: Failure-mode categorization
failure-taxonomy.def: Errors or reasoning traces are coded (manually or by an LLM) into a taxonomy, and their frequencies are compared.
failure-taxonomy.include_if: The output is a distribution over error or behaviour categories.
failure-taxonomy.exclude_if: Performance is broken down by input attributes rather than by error type (stratified-breakdown).

stratified-breakdown.name: Stratified performance breakdown
stratified-breakdown.def: The score or gain is split by difficulty, domain, density, stage or a context factor to find where effects concentrate.
stratified-breakdown.include_if: The same results are re-sliced by an input attribute.
stratified-breakdown.exclude_if: New inputs are constructed to create the strata (controlled-input-injection).

controlled-input-injection.name: Controlled input injection probe
controlled-input-injection.def: Crafted content (distractors, partial guidance, attack payloads, decomposition prompts) is inserted into inputs to test a specific behavioural capacity.
controlled-input-injection.include_if: The inputs are deliberately constructed to elicit and measure one behaviour.
controlled-input-injection.exclude_if: The goal is graded robustness to generic noise (input-perturbation-stress-test).

case-study-walkthrough.name: Qualitative case study / post-mortem
case-study-walkthrough.def: A small number of trajectories, incidents or attacks are walked through in detail and mapped to explanatory principles.
case-study-walkthrough.include_if: The evidence is narrative analysis of a few instances.
case-study-walkthrough.exclude_if: The instances are aggregated into counts (failure-taxonomy).

metric-and-judge-validation.name: Metric or judge agreement with human or ground truth
metric-and-judge-validation.def: Automatic metrics, LLM judges or pipeline detectors are correlated with human labels or held-out ground truth.
metric-and-judge-validation.include_if: The output is an agreement or correlation statistic for an evaluator.
metric-and-judge-validation.exclude_if: A theory-motivated mediator is correlated with performance (targeted-quantity-check).

leakage-and-shortcut-control.name: Leakage, contamination and shortcut control
leakage-and-shortcut-control.def: The design tests whether results come from answer leakage, memorisation, self-sampling bias or shortcut questions.
leakage-and-shortcut-control.include_if: A named contamination path is measured or removed.
leakage-and-shortcut-control.exclude_if: A confound inside the method's own mechanism is isolated (confound-isolating-control).

dataset-characterization-audit.name: Dataset characterization and audit
dataset-characterization-audit.def: Descriptive statistics, difficulty comparisons or manual audits establish the properties and quality of a dataset.
dataset-characterization-audit.include_if: The subject of the experiment is a dataset, not a model.
dataset-characterization-audit.exclude_if: Models are scored on the dataset (many-model-leaderboard).

claim_type.title: What it tests
claim_type.q: What kind of claim does the experiment test? One primary, optionally one secondary. Do not mirror the design (a head-to-head table is comparative-performance only).

comparative-performance.name: Better than others
comparative-performance.def: ours is better than, matches, or is not worse than alternatives

efficiency.name: Efficiency
efficiency.def: needs less data, compute, memory, latency or parameters

scaling.name: Scaling
scaling.def: how behaviour changes with scale; a functional form or extrapolation

generalization.name: Generalization
generalization.def: holds on new domains, tasks, lengths, backbones or held-out conditions

robustness.name: Robustness
robustness.def: holds under noise, corruption, attack, seeds or hyperparameters; includes calibration

attribution.name: Attribution
attribution.def: a specific component or choice is responsible for the gain (credit assignment to parts of the method)

mechanism.name: Mechanism
mechanism.def: an explanation via internal representations, dynamics or a causal process (why, not which part)

theory-validation.name: Theory check
theory-validation.def: an empirical check of a theoretical prediction or assumption

phenomenon.name: Phenomenon
phenomenon.def: an exploratory observation or characterization of a behaviour

negative.name: Negative result
negative.def: something does not help, fails, or a prior claim does not hold

measurement-validity.name: Measurement validity
measurement-validity.def: the metric, judge, dataset or evaluation itself is valid (agreement with humans, no leakage)

safety-security.name: Safety and security
safety-security.def: safety, alignment, attacks, fairness or privacy properties

human-quality.name: Human judgement
human-quality.def: people prefer or rate the output higher

controls.title: Controls
controls.q: Which controls does the paper STATE for this experiment? Only list what is stated; this axis records rigour.

matched-compute.name: Matched compute
matched-compute.def: FLOPs, time, tokens, steps or calls held equal across arms

matched-capacity.name: Matched capacity
matched-capacity.def: parameters or model size held equal

matched-data.name: Matched data
matched-data.def: the same training data across arms

matched-tuning.name: Matched tuning
matched-tuning.def: baselines tuned with the same budget or protocol

same-backbone.name: Same backbone
same-backbone.def: all arms share a base model or architecture

official-baselines.name: Official baselines
official-baselines.def: baselines run from official code or reported numbers with matched settings

random-control.name: Random control
random-control.def: a random or null replacement (random subspace, shuffled labels, random features)

oracle-bound.name: Oracle or bound
oracle-bound.def: an oracle, upper bound or trivial lower-bound baseline

significance.name: Significance test
significance.def: statistical test, confidence intervals or bootstrap

held-out-test.name: Held-out test
held-out-test.def: selection on validation data, final results on untouched test data

human-agreement.name: Human agreement
human-agreement.def: automatic scores validated against human labels

visualization.name: Visualization
visualization.def: attention, embedding, attribution or internal visualization

theory-overlay.name: Theory overlay
theory-overlay.def: empirical results overlaid on a theoretical prediction

role.title: Role in the paper
role.q: What role does the experiment play in the paper?

changes_from_v0: 'manipulation' replaced by data-driven design patterns (9 families, 33 patterns); v0 manipulation labels overlapped (hyperparameter vs scale sweep, ablation vs method swap)
new 'controls' axis records what is held fixed, which separates rigorous from loose designs
claim types: efficiency merged; generalization merged; calibration into robustness; new measurement-validity; at most one secondary label
